c.tagline: Rhineland powerhouse of a soaring cathedral, Kolsch and Carnival.

taxi.fareNote: Fares are metered and regulated; Free Now and Uber dispatch the same licensed taxis, so prices are broadly similar and there is little street-hailing outside ranks and stations.

emergency.note: 112 reaches ambulance and fire across the EU; 110 is the direct police line.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Pickpockets work the Hauptbahnhof, cathedral square and Ringe nightlife strip; keep valuables close late at night around the station and Ebertplatz.

hood_desc: The historic core on the Rhine's left bank, dominated by the twin-spired Gothic Cathedral, the Old Town lanes, riverside promenade, breweries and the main museums; the obvious first-timer base.
Cologne's most stylish quarter (Belgisches Viertel), a grid of independent boutiques, design shops, coffee bars and buzzing nightlife around Brusseler Platz and Friesenplatz.
A multicultural, creative district west of the center famous for street art, live-music venues, Turkish and Balkan food and an unpretentious bar and club scene.
A charming, village-like southern quarter (Severinsviertel) of cozy Kolsch pubs, cafes and small squares, with the medieval Severinstorburg gate at its heart.
A modern district across the Rhine built around the Koelnmesse trade fair, the Lanxess Arena and Bahnhof Deutz, with the city's best postcard views back to the cathedral.
lodging: Hotel Mondial am Dom Cologne - MGallery

water.note: Tap water is safe and strictly regulated.

transit.hours: The Stadtbahn and S-Bahn run roughly 4am-1am, with several lines running all night on Friday and Saturday; night buses fill the gaps midweek.
transit.pay: No transit card needed: buy tickets in the KVB app or from station and on-board machines (bank cards accepted) and keep them for inspection. A single ride in the city is about 3.20 EUR (~US$3.50) and a day ticket around 8 EUR on the VRS tariff; one ticket covers the Stadtbahn, S-Bahn and buses. Staying weeks? The Deutschland-Ticket (58 EUR/month) covers local transit nationwide.

landmarks: Cologne Cathedral (Kölner Dom)
Germany's most visited monument, this staggering UNESCO Gothic cathedral with 157-meter twin spires took 632 years to finish and shelters the golden Shrine of the Three Kings.
Hohenzollern Bridge
Thousands of love locks weight the railings of this triple-arched rail bridge, whose river crossing delivers the definitive postcard view of the Dom.
Great St. Martin Church and the Old Town
The mighty Romanesque tower of Great St. Martin rises over the Altstadt's pastel gabled houses and brauhaus taverns along the Rhine embankment.
Museum Ludwig
Beside the cathedral, one of Europe's great modern art museums holds masterworks by Picasso, Warhol, and the world's finest Pop Art collection outside America.
Romano-Germanic Museum (Römisch-Germanisches Museum)
Built over the famous Dionysus mosaic, this collection of Roman Cologne's glass, tombs, and mosaics ranks among the world's best of its kind.
Chocolate Museum (Schokoladenmuseum)
On a ship-shaped Rheinauhafen peninsula, Lindt's beloved museum traces cocoa from Maya ritual to modern confection, complete with a flowing chocolate fountain.
KölnTriangle observation deck
The glass-ringed rooftop platform across the Rhine in Deutz serves the classic panorama of the cathedral, bridges, and old town skyline.
Wallraf-Richartz Museum
Cologne's oldest museum spans medieval panel painting to Impressionism, with the world's largest collection of the medieval Cologne school of painters.
Rheinauhafen and the Kranhäuser (Crane Houses)
Three inverted-L glass towers echoing harbor cranes define Cologne's regenerated marina quarter, a striking modern counterpoint to the Gothic skyline.
4711 House of Fragrances (Glockengasse)
The neo-Gothic flagship of the original Eau de Cologne, where a carillon plays hourly and visitors can sample the 1792 fragrance that named a city's export.

train.note: Trains leave from Koln Hauptbahnhof, right beside the cathedral, though some ICE services use Koln Messe/Deutz across the river. Frequent ICE services reach Frankfurt (~1h), Frankfurt Airport (~50 min) and Berlin (~4h15), and Brussels is about 1h50 on Eurostar. Eurostar and DB sell the Brussels route on separate fare systems that are not interchangeable, so compare both; Eurostar fares open around six months out. OeBB Nightjet sleepers from Amsterdam to Vienna, Innsbruck and Switzerland call here late in the evening.

bus.note: Long-distance coaches use the Fernbusterminal at Breslauer Platz on the north side of the Hauptbahnhof, which has shelters, machines and toilets. Tickets are cheapest online; walk-up fares are noticeably higher. Brussels takes around 4h, Amsterdam about 4h30 and Paris roughly 8h, so the coach mainly wins on price rather than time.

intl.to: Dusseldorf, Bonn, Konigswinter & the Middle Rhine (Germany) - sails from the Frankenwerft landing stages below the Altstadt

ferry.note: Cologne is far inland on the Rhine and has no sea ferry. KD, which is headquartered in the city, runs panorama cruises and scheduled Rhine sailings from the Frankenwerft quay right below the cathedral, including day trips downstream to Dusseldorf and Zons and upstream towards Bonn and the Siebengebirge. Most services run from spring to autumn, with Advent and New Year specials in winter. River-cruise ships also berth along the Rheinauhafen and Frankenwerft.
